o.text: From Proto-Turkic *eĺčgek (“donkey”). Cognate with Turkish eşek, Chuvash ашак (aš̬ak), etc. Similarity with Armenian էշ (ēš), իշակ (išak) is a coincidence.
From Proto-Turkic *koŕï. Cognate with Turkish kuzu, Kazakh қозы (qozı), Turkmen guzy, etc.
Inherited from Proto-Turkic *āb-lag. Synchronically analysable as ov (“hunt”) + -laq. Compare Turkish avlak, Turkmen āwlag, Uzbek ovloq.
Borrowed from Persian آزوای (āzvāy, “a species of black, bitter Indian erath, which draws the noxius humours from sores and swellings”), whence also Turkish azvay, Northern Kurdish ezva.
